excerpts.author: trent_vanepps
excerpts.content:
for anyone catching up, this is the latest on status for many parts of 1559:

https://eipupdate.substack.com/p/eip-update-issue-1-eip-1559

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: I just left a couple comments on https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2505/files

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: minor spec stuff involving the `//` symbol and cleaner presentation

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content: Our team will try and help move this EIP forward as well. It may be worth trying to setup a call over the next few weeks to see what needs to be done next and where our team can be most helpful. Our biggest open question right now is whether we should start working on a second implementation in Besu, try and help out with the geth implementation/spec or something else completely.

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: high level question: what is the next concrete target for the whole process?

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: My instinct would be: we want EIP 1559 running on some testnet that some people actually use ASAP

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content:
Yes, that's what I'm trying to understand as well. My rough roadmap was:
1. Finish Geth (and Besu) implementation, make sure the spec is updated.
2. (controversial) Fork Ropsten to get a mining testnet running EIP-1559 that already has a large existing state
3. Figure out what breaks in production 🙂

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: that seems reasonable

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: hopefully with an eye to getting it live on *the* ropsten

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content: Yeah, I think that would be step 4. IMO a 1559-focused testnet (even if short lived) means we can likely ship sooner and experiment more.

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: yeah, agree that makes sense as step 2

excerpts.author: madeof_tin7509
excerpts.content: I have been thinking since our conversation yesterday Tim. You all (besu) working on an implementation that can be deployed on a testnet would be best to focus efforts on.

excerpts.author: madeof_tin7509

excerpts.author: madeof_tin7509
excerpts.content: If we can have a Geth and Besu implementation running together on a testnet I think a lot of things will get shaken out between those two and that can inform any final spec. It also gives us something to do any economic analysis on.
